Those are clearly different (seed and leaf diseases). The test image shows a mature soybean stem and pods with numerous small black specks (pycnidia) on the stem surface, with some appearing in linear arrangements along the stem. This is the hallmark of Diaporthe (pod and stem blight).

Key evidence:
- Small black raised specks (pycnidia) on mature stem surface and pods
- Specks appear in somewhat linear rows on the stem
- Plant is at mature/harvest stage
- No internal charcoal-like microsclerotia (rules out Charcoal Rot)
- Specks are individual dots, not the "pin cushion" acervuli of Anthracnose
